clue.text: Odd article in Le Monde showing lack of sophistication

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, as printed in a paper like Le Monde
common means vulgar or unrefined

explanation.surface: A strange piece in a French newspaper reveals the writer's naivety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd article' reads as one phrase, but the split falls after Odd: the definition is that single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon is unusual or rare, which is what odd means as an adjective.

clue.text: Releases elite US troops to support peacekeeping force

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits underneath it, so the troops come second

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
the Navy SEALs are an elite American special forces unit

explanation.surface: American special forces are sent to back up a UN peacekeeping mission.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseal a letter or document is to open it, so it releases what was shut inside.

clue.text: Make a detailed plan of church painting and sculpture?

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
painting and sculpture are both forms of art

explanation.surface: Someone sketches out a scheme for decorating a church with pictures and statues.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart something is to map it out carefully, as on a navigator's map.

clue.text: One unable to shut up car opening

parts.note: a motor is an informal word for a car
a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: Someone cannot manage to close up a car door or boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like closing the car, but in the definition it means stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A motormouth is an informal term for a compulsive talker who never stops chattering.

clue.text: Highly decorated knight coming in to deliver speech

indicators.note: the knight enters the other word, ending up inside it

parts.note: to orate is to make a formal speech
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A much-medalled knight arrives to give an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly decorated' suggests medals on a knight, but here it means elaborately ornamented.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate describes something lavishly embellished with elaborate ornamentation.

clue.text: Prominent piece of land held by businessman

indicators.note: the word is held inside the letters of the following word

parts.note: the letters run inside busi-___-man

explanation.surface: A tycoon owns a notable plot of real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland or promontory jutting out into the sea, as in place names like Loch Ness's shores.

clue.text: English vicar's first financial backer for any of the Gospels

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the vicar

parts.note: the initial of vicar
an angel is someone who invests money in a venture, especially a theatre show

explanation.surface: An English clergyman's main donor pays for copies of the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an archaic word for gospel, and so any of the four Gospel books.

clue.text: Exhausted writer found in street

indicators.note: the writer is located inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A worn-out author is discovered lying in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the pen that writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, drained of all energy, the same as exhausted.

clue.text: Line is removed from shocking opening

indicators.note: removal tells us to take the line abbreviation out of the next word

parts.note: startling means surprising or shocking
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A line is cut from an outrageous first scene.
explanation.walkthrough: STARTLING loses its L to give STARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting move or gambit is an opening one, the first in a sequence.

clue.text: Podcaster's way of running portal

indicators.note: a podcast is heard, not read, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking or running

explanation.surface: A podcaster explains how to run a website portal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an entrance or doorway, which is what a portal literally is.

clue.text: Roaming on coast via Canadian province

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters wander from their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller wanders along the seaboard by way of a Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's Maritime provinces, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Following source of financial news during tumultuous era

indicators.note: during puts the news source inside the period of time that follows
tumultuous means disordered, so the letters of era are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
the FT is the Financial Times, a British business newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone tracks the money pages through a turbulent period in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' looks like a first-letter signal, but the whole source is the newspaper, the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: After and following both mean coming later in time or sequence.

clue.text: However, idiot finally had an idea

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'he came, though'

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of idiot

parts.note: the last letter of idiot

explanation.surface: Despite everything, the fool at last came up with a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is the past tense of think, and to think of something is to have an idea.

clue.text: Salt spring?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to add salt or other flavouring to food
second meaning: one of the four quarters of the year

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a salty mineral spring, but the two words are separate meanings: one a verb, one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it with salt, and spring is one of the year's four periods.

clue.text: Leader of American party unconcerned about others

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, so only the opening of American is kept

parts.note: the first letter of American
a social is an informal party or gathering

explanation.surface: The head of a US political party doesn't care about anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but here it is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding or indifferent to the company and interests of other people.

clue.text: Everyone in Slough yielded to temptation

indicators.note: in places the word for everyone inside the marshland word

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog, and a fen is marshy ground
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole population of the English town of Slough gave in to sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town near London, but the capital letter misleads: a slough is a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen describes someone who has sinned or lost moral standing, as in a fallen woman or angel.

clue.text: How to identify someone 9 staff upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: the answer to 9 across
to man something is to staff it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about naming someone whose employees are disgruntled.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a badge worn to show who a person is, letting others identify them.

clue.text: Stick plug in this place

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to push a plug into a socket right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests a stopper or socket, but it is the slang sense of a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast, whether glue to paper or a person to a rule.

clue.text: Fool regularly ignored trendy set

parts.note: a clot is a British informal word for a stupid person

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means skipping every other letter of trendy

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of trendy

explanation.surface: A silly person keeps being snubbed by the fashionable crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun for the in-crowd, but it is the verb meaning thickened.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted means thickened into lumps, as cream or blood does when it has set.

clue.text: Crude bombs made better

indicators.note: bombs blow things apart, so the letters of the first word are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Primitive explosives turned out to be an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured means healed of an illness, so restored to health and made well again.

clue.text: Best part of dairy product

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the fatty liquid that rises to the top of milk

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the best bit of some milky food; 'of' simply links two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The richest layer of milk rises to the top, so the word also names the elite of any group.

clue.text: Resin obtained from bio-fuel emissions

indicators.note: the letters are extracted from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across bio-fu-___-ssions, starting at the end of fuel

explanation.surface: A tree gum is extracted from the exhaust of biofuels.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant tropical tree resin used in varnishes, inks and perfumes.

clue.text: Control time in office for auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the phrase is what a hearer takes in

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's period in power

explanation.surface: Limiting a term of office for a financial auditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a strap for guiding a horse, so figuratively a means of restraint or control.

clue.text: Smashed TV set screening men's formal attire

indicators.note: a screen encloses what it hides, so the rearranged letters go around the men
something smashed is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the possessive

explanation.surface: A broken television is showing a programme about men's evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' suggests a TV showing something; here it means shielding, placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe or garment, especially one worn by clergy during services.

clue.text: First person guided around shop

indicators.note: turned around means read the pieces from the other end

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
led means guided

explanation.surface: The narrator was shown round a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' tempts a first letter, but it is the pronoun I.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Reprimanding despicable person's boring existence

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the despicable person tunnels inside existence

parts.note: being means existence
a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Telling off a nasty character for leading such a dull life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling through.
explanation.definitionFit: Berating means scolding or criticising someone angrily at length.
